properties.name: CEA-Leti
properties.description:
**CEA-Leti** — CEA-Leti (Laboratoire d'électronique des technologies de l'information), Grenoble (FR)

One of the world's largest applied research organizations in microelectronics and nanotechnology, established 1967 in Grenoble. Operates 200mm and 300mm CMOS lines, a 200mm MEMS line, a 300mm photonics platform, and a 300mm 3D integration line across 11,000 m2 of ISO 9001-certified cleanroom space. ~1,900 employees, 286+ patents granted per year.

**Why it's on this map:** Large-scale MEMS and 3D-integration fabrication capability -- a potential (likely enterprise-scale rather than cheap/startup-friendly) route to getting small custom devices actually manufactured.

[[https://www.leti-cea.com/cea-tech/leti/english/Pages/Welcome.aspx|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: ChipFoundry.io
properties.description:
**ChipFoundry.io** — ChipFoundry, San Francisco Bay Area, CA (US)

Chip design and fabrication service built on SkyWater 130nm with an open-source PDK and open-source toolchain, offering chipIgnite tapeouts at $14,950 plus an educational chipDiscover program. Founded by former Efabless leadership (Jeff DiCorpo, Mohamed Kassem) after Efabless shut down in early 2025, re-enabling the same SkyWater 130 access route the open-source silicon community had relied on.

**Why it's on this map:** Offers an accessible, open-source-toolchain route to fabricating custom chips on a mature process node -- directly useful infrastructure for getting a small custom chip made cheaply, especially after a prior well-known low-cost access route in this space shut down.

[[https://chipfoundry.io/|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Brazilian Nanotechnology National Laboratory (LNNano)
properties.description:
**Brazilian Nanotechnology National Laboratory (LNNano)** — Centro Nacional de Pesquisa em Energia e Materiais (CNPEM), Campinas (BR)

Brazilian national nanotechnology laboratory operating open-access cleanroom facilities (ISO 6/7-class) for micro- and nanofabrication -- photolithography, e-beam lithography, PVD/sputtering -- supporting MEMS, microfluidic lab-on-a-chip devices, optical/chemical sensors, and RF devices. Open to external researchers via a competitive facility-use proposal process, the same access model as europractice/ihp-cleanroom.

**Why it's on this map:** Open-access national cleanroom for micro- and nanofabrication (photolithography, e-beam lithography, MEMS) -- a genuine potential fabrication route, and one of the only such open facilities identified in South America.

[[https://lnnano.cnpem.br/en/home-en/|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
properties.institution: Centro Nacional de Pesquisa em Energia e Materiais (CNPEM)

properties.name: EUROPRACTICE
properties.description:
**EUROPRACTICE** — EUROPRACTICE (imec-coordinated consortium), Leuven (BE)

European Commission-launched consortium (since 1995) of five research organizations, led by imec, providing academia and industry with affordable Multi-Project-Wafer (MPW) prototyping across a wide range of processes -- digital, RF, mixed-signal, high-voltage ASICs, MEMS, photonics, microfluidics, flexible electronics, compound semiconductors -- plus ~65,000 concurrent EDA tool licenses distributed to European universities annually and training programs.

**Why it's on this map:** A European multi-project-wafer consortium giving academia and industry affordable access to chip and MEMS fabrication -- genuinely useful shared infrastructure for getting a small custom chip or device made without enterprise-scale cost.

[[https://europractice-ic.com/|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Fraunhofer IPMS
properties.description:
**Fraunhofer IPMS** — Fraunhofer Institute for Photonic Microsystems, Dresden (DE)

Applied research institute for photonic and electronic microsystems, nanoelectronics, microdisplays, and wireless data communication. Operates a 1500 m2, ISO 14644-1 class 4 MOEMS/MEMS cleanroom supporting technology development up to pilot production on 200 mm wafers, plus wafer processing, characterization/test, and packaging/interconnection services. One of only two German research institutions -- alongside Fraunhofer IZM-ASSID -- with 300 mm wafer capability.

**Why it's on this map:** Operates a large MEMS/microsystems cleanroom with rare 300mm wafer capability -- a substantial, in-region potential fabrication route for microscale mechanical components.

[[https://www.ipms.fraunhofer.de/en.html|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: IHP Research & Prototyping Service
properties.description:
**René Scholz** — IHP – Leibniz-Institut für innovative Mikroelektronik, Frankfurt (Oder) (DE)

Research & Prototyping Service
The Research & Prototyping Service group coordinates service and industry relevant development activities within Technology Department.

Please check our website for details or contact us directly to discuss your special request.

Multi Project Wafer Runs with 0.13 and 0.25 μm SiGe BiCMOS technologies and Silicon Photonics technologies are regularly organized. Here new technologies can be used in research and benchmarking projects. Stable technologies are offered for development projects towards functional prototypes.

Our stable and qualified technologies are also available as foundry service for low volume production via IHP Solutions.

To support customer developments, we offer wafer-level measurements from device level to functional testing of complex analog and digital circuits.

IHP has a wide range of failure mode analysis and analytical diagnostics equipment that can be offered to support customer projects.

If you are missing special features or need dedicated wafer preparations based on Si technology, we offer a technology development service that goes beyond our standard offerings. This includes developments of single process steps up to modules and adaptations of existing technologies.

To apply our technologies and developments to high-volume production, IHP offers technology transfer to commercial foundries.

**Why it's on this map:** Operates a cleanroom offering a mature, open-PDK-compatible chip fabrication process -- a genuinely usable, relatively low-cost route to getting a small custom chip actually manufactured.

[[https://www.ihp-microelectronics.com/services/research-and-prototyping-service|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Laboratorio Nacional de Nanoelectrónica — Microelectronics Laboratory
properties.description:
**Laboratorio Nacional de Nanoelectrónica — Microelectronics Laboratory** — Instituto Nacional de Astrofísica, Óptica y Electrónica (INAOE), Puebla (MX)

Mexico's only laboratory capable of fabricating integrated circuits from silicon wafers, using CMOS/NMOS/bipolar processes plus PECVD and sol-gel deposition to build MEMS, sensors, bolometers, and solar cells. Operating since 1974, it serves as both a national fabrication resource and a graduate training facility in semiconductor device physics.

**Why it's on this map:** The only laboratory in its country capable of fabricating integrated circuits from silicon wafers -- a national-scale fabrication resource of the same kind (chip/MEMS access) as other cleanroom-service entries on this map, just in a region that previously had none.

[[https://www-elec.inaoep.mx/laboratorios/microelectronica|Group website]]

Category: Clean Room Service · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
